title: Uniform convergence is closed under termwise addition
statement: If F converges uniformly to G on [a,b] and H converges uniformly to K on [a,b], then the termwise sum (fun n x => F n x + H n x) converges uniformly on [a,b] to the pointwise sum (fun x => G x + K x). The proof rearranges a four-term sum (two convergence gaps) via add4_comm so the two gap terms land together, fuses the two ofRat-embedded rational gaps into one via CReal.ofRat_add, rebuilds a single close_within bound via CReal.abs_le_of_two_sided, and widens that bound by an exact Rat equality (Rat.natDivSucc_add) to the stated combined rate.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.uniform_converges_add : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> CReal))) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> CReal))) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x4 : CReal) -> ((x5 : CReal) -> ((x6 : CReal.UniformConvergesOn x0 x2 x4 x5) -> ((x7 : CReal.UniformConvergesOn x1 x3 x4 x5) -> CReal.UniformConvergesOn (fun (x8 : AxNat) => fun (x9 : CReal) => CReal.add (x0 x8 x9) (x1 x8 x9)) (fun (x8 : CReal) => CReal.add (x2 x8) (x3 x8)) x4 x5))))))))
